definition: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that decomposes pretrained weights into magnitude and direction components, then applies LoRA to the direction component for improved learning behavior.
details: DoRA analyzes the difference between full fine-tuning and LoRA and finds that LoRA lacks the negative directional-magnitude correlation seen in full fine-tuning. By learning magnitude separately and using low-rank updates for direction, DoRA improves accuracy and training stability over LoRA. It has been integrated into libraries such as PEFT and can be merged into the base weights.
